input.body:
label: bug
file: src/ingest/parser.ts

The parser splits the uploaded file on `"
"` only (see `lines = text.split("
")`), so it doesn't account for Windows-style `
` line endings. Since the finance team's new Windows export tool likely emits `
`, the trailing `` ends up attached to the last column of each row (including the header), which breaks the column-count comparison and triggers the `errors.rowShape` ("Malformed row") error on row 1. The parser should normalize/strip `` characters (or split on `/
|
/`) before comparing row lengths.

text: The root cause is in `src/ingest/parser.ts`, which splits CSV content using `"\n"` only (not handling Windows `\r\n` line endings), causing column count mismatches when parsing files exported from the new Windows tool.
